title: Lighting Technicians
description: Set up, maintain, and dismantle light fixtures, lighting control devices, and the associated lighting electrical and rigging equipment used for photography, television, film, video, and live productions. May focus or operate light fixtures, or attach color filters or other lighting accessories.

tasks.text: Disassemble and store equipment after performances.
Install color effects or image patterns, such as color filters, onto lighting fixtures.
Install electrical cables or wire fixtures.
Match light fixture settings, such as brightness and color, to lighting design plans.
Patch or wire lights to dimmers or other electronic consoles.
Set up and focus light fixtures to meet requirements of television, theater, concerts, or other productions.
Set up scaffolding or cranes to assist with setting up of lighting equipment.
Assess safety of wiring or equipment set-up to determine the risk of fire or electrical shock.
Test lighting equipment function and desired lighting effects.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Consult with lighting director or production staff to determine lighting requirements.
Notify supervisors when major lighting equipment repairs are needed.
Load, unload, or position lighting equipment.
Operate manual or automated systems to control lighting throughout productions.
Perform minor repairs or routine maintenance on lighting equipment, such as replacing lamps or damaged color filters.
Program lighting consoles or load automated lighting control systems onto consoles.
Visit and assess structural and electrical layout of locations before setting up lighting equipment.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: FileMaker Pro, Microsoft Access.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Autodesk AutoCAD.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.
